chapters.title: Hannah's Prayer and Samuel's Birth
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 1

Elkanah's Two Wives

1There was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Elkanah son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.

2He had two wives. The name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.

3This man used to go up from his town year by year to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD there.

4And it came to pass, on the day Elkanah sacrificed, that he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.

5But to Hannah he would give a double portion, for he loved Hannah, though the LORD had closed her womb.

6Her rival used to provoke her severely to make her fret, because the LORD had closed her womb.

7So it went on year after year: as often as she went up to the house of the LORD, the other provoked her, and she wept and would not eat.

8Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? Why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"

The Vow

9After they had eaten and drunk at Shiloh, Hannah rose. Eli the priest was sitting on the seat beside the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

10She was bitter of soul, and she prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.

11She made a vow and said, "LORD of hosts, if You will indeed look on the affliction of Your servant and remember me, and not forget Your servant, but give Your servant a male child, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall go up on his head."

12As she kept on praying before the LORD, Eli was watching her mouth.

13Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. So Eli thought she was drunk.

14Eli said to her, "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine from you."

15But Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.

16Do not take your servant for a worthless woman, for I have been speaking all this time out of my great distress and provocation."

17Eli answered, "Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant the request you have asked of Him."

18She said, "Let your servant find favor in your eyes." Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.

Samuel

19They rose early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD, then went back to their house at Ramah. Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.

20And it came to pass in due time that Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, "Because I asked him of the LORD."

21The man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and his vow.

22But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "Not until the boy is weaned. Then I will bring him, so that he may appear before the LORD and stay there forever."

23Elkanah her husband said to her, "Do what seems good in your eyes. Stay until you have weaned him. Only may the LORD establish His word." So the woman stayed and nursed her son until she weaned him.

24When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. The boy was young.

25They slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to Eli.

26She said, "Please, my lord! As you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here beside you, praying to the LORD.

27For this boy I prayed, and the LORD has granted me the request I asked of Him.

28So I, too, have lent him to the LORD. All the days that he lives he is lent to the LORD." Then they worshiped the LORD there.

Notes

  • v3 "the LORD of hosts" — YHWH tseva'ot, and this is its first occurrence in the Bible. Tseva'ot are armies, the ranks of heaven and of Israel. The same root names the women who served in ranks at the tent of meeting (Exodus 38:8), who return in 2:22. Hannah is the first person to pray to God by this name (v11).

  • v5 "a double portion" — manah achat appayim, one portion, of two faces. The phrase is not found elsewhere, and its sense is uncertain; the usual reading is a double or worthy portion. The Greek has one portion, because she had no child, though Elkanah loved Hannah more than the other.

  • v6 "Her rival" — tsaratah, the word for a second wife, from the root of distress. Leviticus 18:18 forbids taking two sisters as a rival; the story of Rachel and Leah showed why.

  • v11 "look on the affliction of Your servant… no razor shall go up on his head" — the words of Leah, the LORD has seen my affliction (Genesis 29:32), and of the LORD at the bush (Exodus 3:7). No razor shall go up on his head is the promise to Samson's mother (Judges 13:5), made here by the mother herself as a vow. The Greek adds and wine and strong drink he shall not drink, the other half of the Nazirite law (Numbers 6:3).

  • vv12–13 "speaking in her heart; only her lips moved" — Abraham's servant spoke to my heart before Rebekah came out (Genesis 24:45), but this is the first prayer in which a voice is expressly not heard. Eli, the priest at the house of the LORD, cannot tell it from drunkenness.

  • v16 "a worthless woman" — bat beliyya'al, daughter of worthlessness. The next chapter uses the same phrase of Eli's own sons (2:12).

  • vv20, 27, 28 "I asked him… lent to the LORD" — the verb sha'al, ask, runs through the chapter: the request you have asked (v17), I asked him of the LORD (v20), I have lent him, hish'iltihu, and he is lent, sha'ul (v28). Sha'ul is the name Saul. The name Samuel is explained by the verb that spells Saul's name, and the two men's stories will be bound together.

  • v23 "may the LORD establish His word" — no word of the LORD has been reported. The Greek has may the Lord establish what has come out of your mouth, Hannah's vow. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v24 "a three-year-old bull" — the Hebrew has three bulls, but v25 says they slaughtered the bull, one. The Greek has a three-year-old calf. The text follows the Greek, which v25 confirms.

  • v24 "The boy was young" — ve-ha-na'ar na'ar, and the boy was a boy: still a small child when he is left at Shiloh.

chapters.title: Hannah's Song, and the Sons of Eli
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 2

Hannah's Song

1Then Hannah prayed and said:

My heart exults in the LORD;
my horn is lifted high in the LORD.
My mouth is wide open over my enemies,
for I rejoice in Your salvation.

2There is none holy like the LORD,
for there is none besides You;
there is no rock like our God.

3Do not keep talking so very proudly;
let no arrogance come from your mouth,
for the LORD is a God of knowledge,
and by Him actions are weighed.

4The bows of the mighty are broken,
and those who stumbled are girded with strength.

5Those who were full hire themselves out for bread,
and those who were hungry hunger no more.
The barren has borne seven,
and she who has many children languishes.

6The LORD puts to death and makes alive;
He brings down to Sheol and brings up.

7The LORD makes poor and makes rich;
He brings low; He also lifts up.

8He raises the poor from the dust;
He lifts the needy from the ash heap,
to seat them with nobles
and make them inherit a seat of honor.
For the pillars of the earth are the LORD's,
and He has set the world on them.

9He guards the feet of His faithful ones,
but the wicked are silenced in darkness,
for not by strength shall a man prevail.

10The LORD — those who contend with Him are shattered;
against them He thunders in the heavens.
The LORD judges the ends of the earth.
He gives strength to His king
and lifts high the horn of His anointed.

The Sons of Eli

11Then Elkanah went home to Ramah, and the boy ministered to the LORD before Eli the priest.

12The sons of Eli were worthless men; they did not know the LORD.

13The custom of the priests with the people was this: whenever anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest's servant would come while the meat was boiling, with a three-pronged fork in his hand,

14and he would thrust it into the pan or kettle or cauldron or pot. All that the fork brought up the priest would take for himself. This is what they did to all Israel who came there to Shiloh.

15Even before the fat was burned, the priest's servant would come and say to the man who was sacrificing, "Give meat for the priest to roast. He will not take boiled meat from you, only raw."

16If the man said to him, "Let them burn the fat first, and then take as much as you wish," he would say, "No, you must give it now, and if not, I will take it by force."

17So the sin of the young men was very great before the LORD, for the men treated the offering of the LORD with contempt.

Samuel at Shiloh

18Samuel was ministering before the LORD, a boy clothed with a linen ephod.

19His mother would make him a little robe and bring it up to him year by year, when she went up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.

20Eli would bless Elkanah and his wife and say, "May the LORD give you children by this woman in place of the one she asked for and lent to the LORD." Then they would go back to their home.

21The LORD visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The boy Samuel grew up before the LORD.

22Eli was very old. He heard all that his sons were doing to all Israel, and how they lay with the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

23He said to them, "Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.

24No, my sons; it is not a good report that I hear the people of the LORD spreading.

25If one man sins against another, God will mediate for him; but if a man sins against the LORD, who can intercede for him?" But they would not listen to the voice of their father, for the LORD wished to put them to death.

26The boy Samuel kept growing in stature and in favor, both with the LORD and with men.

A Man of God

27A man of God came to Eli and said to him, "Thus says the LORD: 'Did I not reveal Myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt, subject to the house of Pharaoh?

28I chose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be My priest, to go up to My altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before Me, and I gave to the house of your father all the offerings by fire of the sons of Israel.

29Why then do you kick at My sacrifice and My offering, which I commanded for My dwelling, and honor your sons above Me by fattening yourselves on the choicest parts of every offering of Israel My people?'

30Therefore the LORD, the God of Israel, declares: 'I did say that your house and the house of your father would walk before Me forever.' But now the LORD declares: 'Far be it from Me! For those who honor Me I will honor, and those who despise Me shall be lightly esteemed.

31The days are coming when I will cut off your strength and the strength of your father's house, so that there will not be an old man in your house.

32You will see distress in My dwelling, in all the good that He does for Israel, and there shall not be an old man in your house forever.

33The man of yours whom I do not cut off from My altar shall be spared to wear out your eyes and grieve your soul, and all the increase of your house shall die as men.

34This shall be the sign to you, which shall come on your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas: on one day both of them shall die.

35I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest, who shall do according to what is in My heart and in My soul. I will build him a sure house, and he shall walk before My anointed forever.

36And it shall come to pass that everyone who is left in your house shall come to bow down to him for a piece of silver or a loaf of bread, and shall say, "Please put me in one of the priest's places, so that I may eat a piece of bread."'"

Notes

  • vv1, 10 "my horn is lifted high… the horn of His anointed" — qeren, the horn of an animal, the Bible's picture of strength. The song opens with Hannah's horn and closes with the horn of His anointed, meshicho, the first time the word mashiach is used of a king, though Israel has no king yet. The Greek has christou autou.

  • v2 "there is no rock like our God" — tsur, the name of God in the Song of Moses: The Rock — His work is whole (Deuteronomy 32:4).

  • v3 "by Him actions are weighed" — the written text has lo, not: actions are not weighed. The reading tradition has lo, by Him, and the Greek, a God preparing His ways, agrees with it; the two words sound alike. The text follows the reading.

  • v5 "The barren has borne seven" — Hannah will have six children (v21); seven is the full number, as in better to you than seven sons (Ruth 4:15).

  • v6 "The LORD puts to death and makes alive" — the words of Deuteronomy 32:39, I put to death and I make alive. Sheol is the place of the dead.

  • vv7–8 "He brings low; He also lifts up… He raises the poor from the dust" — Mary's song in Luke 1:52–53 takes up the same reversal: He has brought down rulers from thrones and lifted up the lowly; the hungry He has filled with good things. The Greek of 1 Samuel 2:10 adds a passage found in Jeremiah 9:23–24, Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom… but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows the Lord.

  • vv13–16 "the custom of the priests" — the law gave the priest the breast that is waved and the thigh after the fat was burned (Leviticus 7:31, 34), for all fat belongs to the LORD (3:16). Eli's sons take their share with a fork before the LORD's part is burned, and by force.

  • v25 "for the LORD wished to put them to death" — ki chafets YHWH lahamitam. Their refusal to listen is tied to the LORD's purpose, as Pharaoh's hardened heart was. God will mediate, u-fillelo Elohim, and who can intercede, yitpallel, are the same root, the root of prayer.

  • v26 "in stature and in favor, both with the LORD and with men" — Luke 2:52 says the same of the boy Jesus: in wisdom and stature and in favor with God and men.

  • vv29–30 "honor… lightly esteemed" — kavod is weight, and qalal is to be light. Eli honors, gives weight to, his sons over God, and the sons are fattening themselves. 4:18 will say that Eli died because he was old and heavy, kaved.

chapters.title: The LORD Calls Samuel
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 3

The Call

1The boy Samuel was ministering to the LORD before Eli. The word of the LORD was rare in those days; there was no vision breaking through.

2And it came to pass at that time that Eli, whose eyes had begun to grow dim so that he could not see, was lying down in his place.

3The lamp of God had not yet gone out, and Samuel was lying down in the temple of the LORD, where the ark of God was.

4Then the LORD called Samuel, and he said, "Here I am."

5He ran to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." But he said, "I did not call; lie down again." So he went and lay down.

6The LORD called again, "Samuel!" Samuel got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." But he said, "I did not call, my son; lie down again."

7Samuel did not yet know the LORD, and the word of the LORD had not yet been revealed to him.

8The LORD called Samuel again, the third time. He got up and went to Eli and said, "Here I am, for you called me." Then Eli understood that the LORD was calling the boy.

9Eli said to Samuel, "Go, lie down. And it shall come to pass, if He calls you, that you shall say, 'Speak, LORD, for Your servant is listening.'" So Samuel went and lay down in his place.

10The LORD came and stood there and called as at the other times, "Samuel! Samuel!" Samuel said, "Speak, for Your servant is listening."

The Word Against Eli's House

11The LORD said to Samuel, "I am about to do a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.

12On that day I will carry out against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.

13I have told him that I am about to judge his house forever, for the iniquity that he knew, because his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.

14Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever."

15Samuel lay until morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.

16But Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son." He said, "Here I am."

17Eli said, "What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do so to you and more also, if you hide from me anything of all the word that He spoke to you."

18So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. Eli said, "It is the LORD. Let Him do what is good in His eyes."

A Prophet of the LORD

19Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.

20All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of the LORD.

21The LORD appeared again at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

Notes

  • v1 "The word of the LORD was rare" — yaqar, precious, scarce. No vision breaking through, niferats, from parats, to break out, as water or a crowd does.

  • vv2–3 "whose eyes had begun to grow dim… The lamp of God had not yet gone out" — Eli's sight is failing, as Isaac's was (Genesis 27:1), and the lamp that was to burn from evening until morning before the LORD (Exodus 27:21) is still lit: it is the night's last hours, and not yet dark in either sense.

  • vv4, 10 "Here I am… Samuel! Samuel!" — hinneni, the answer of Abraham at the binding of Isaac and of Moses at the bush, and the name called twice, as they were called (Genesis 22:11, Exodus 3:4).

  • v7 "Samuel did not yet know the LORD" — said without blame. Eli's sons did not know the LORD (2:12) and were priests; the boy does not know Him yet, because the word has not come to him.

  • v11 "both ears… will tingle" — titsallenah, the ringing of the ears at news too heavy to hear. 4:12–22 tells the news: the ark taken, both sons dead, Eli dead.

  • v13 "his sons were bringing a curse on themselves… he did not restrain them" — meqallelim lahem. The Greek reads his sons were speaking evil of God, and lahem, themselves, differs from Elohim, God, by two letters. The text follows the Hebrew. Did not restrain, lo kihah, is from the root of Eli's dim eyes in v2: he did not see, and he did not check them.

  • v14 "shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering" — the sons abused the sacrifices (2:13–17), and sacrifice will not cover them.

  • v18 "It is the LORD. Let Him do what is good in His eyes" — Eli accepts the word against his own house without protest.

  • v19 "let none of his words fall to the ground" — every word Samuel spoke came true. The same was said of the LORD's promises to Israel: not one word failed (Joshua 21:45, 23:14).

  • v20 "established as a prophet" — ne'eman, faithful, made sure, the word of the man of God's promise, I will raise up for Myself a faithful priest (2:35). The Greek adds a closing summary: Samuel was trusted as a prophet to all Israel from one end of the earth to the other, while Eli's sons kept to their evil way.

I have told him that I am about to judge his house forever, for the iniquity that he knew, because his sons were bringing a curse on themselves, and he did not restrain them.
Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli's house shall not be atoned for by sacrifice or offering forever."
Samuel lay until morning; then he opened the doors of the house of the LORD. Samuel was afraid to tell the vision to Eli.
But Eli called Samuel and said, "Samuel, my son." He said, "Here I am."
Eli said, "What is the word that He spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. May God do so to you and more also, if you hide from me anything of all the word that He spoke to you."
So Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him. Eli said, "It is the LORD. Let Him do what is good in His eyes."
A Prophet of the LORD
Samuel grew, and the LORD was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground.
All Israel from Dan to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of the LORD.
The LORD appeared again at Shiloh, for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel at Shiloh by the word of the LORD.

chapters.title: The Ark Is Taken
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 4

Aphek

1The word of Samuel came to all Israel. Israel went out to battle against the Philistines. They camped at Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.

2The Philistines drew up in line against Israel, and when the battle spread, Israel was struck down before the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men on the field of battle.

3When the people came to the camp, the elders of Israel said, "Why has the LORD struck us down today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD here from Shiloh, so that it may come among us and save us from the hand of our enemies."

4So the people sent to Shiloh and brought from there the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

5And it came to pass, when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, that all Israel gave a great shout, and the earth rang.

6When the Philistines heard the sound of the shout, they said, "What is this great shouting in the camp of the Hebrews?" And they learned that the ark of the LORD had come into the camp.

7The Philistines were afraid, for they said, "A god has come into the camp." They said, "Woe to us! Nothing like this has happened before.

8Woe to us! Who will deliver us from the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with every kind of plague in the wilderness.

9Take courage and be men, Philistines, or you will serve the Hebrews as they have served you. Be men and fight!"

10So the Philistines fought, and Israel was struck down, and they fled, each to his tent. The slaughter was very great: thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell.

11The ark of God was taken, and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

The News at Shiloh

12A man of Benjamin ran from the battle line and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn and earth on his head.

13When he came, Eli was sitting on his seat beside the road, watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of God. When the man came to tell it in the town, the whole town cried out.

14When Eli heard the sound of the outcry, he said, "What is this uproar?" The man hurried and came and told Eli.

15Eli was ninety-eight years old; his eyes were fixed, and he could not see.

16The man said to Eli, "I am the one who came from the battle line; I fled from the battle line today." He said, "How did it go, my son?"

17The one who brought the news answered, "Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has also been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God has been taken."

18And it came to pass, when he mentioned the ark of God, that Eli fell backward from his seat beside the gate, and his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.

Ichabod

19His daughter-in-law, the wife of Phinehas, was pregnant and about to give birth. When she heard the news that the ark of God was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed down and gave birth, for her pains came upon her.

20As she was dying, the women standing by her said, "Do not be afraid, for you have borne a son." But she did not answer or pay attention.

21She named the boy Ichabod, saying, "The glory has gone into exile from Israel," because the ark of God had been taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

22She said, "The glory has gone into exile from Israel, for the ark of God has been taken."

Notes

  • v1 "Ebenezer" — stone of help. The place gets its name only in 7:12, when Samuel sets up a stone there after a victory; here it is named in advance, at the site of a defeat. The Greek opens the verse with And it came to pass in those days that the Philistines gathered for war against Israel.

  • v3 "so that it may come among us and save us" — the Hebrew verbs can be read it or He. The elders speak as though the ark were the LORD, and as though bringing it would oblige Him. The LORD Himself says nothing in the chapter.

  • v4 "the LORD of hosts, who is enthroned on the cherubim" — yoshev ha-keruvim, the first time the title is given. The cherubim are the two on the cover of the ark, from between the two cherubim where the LORD said He would speak (Exodus 25:22).

  • v6 "the Hebrews" — ivrim, the name the Egyptians used for Israel (Exodus 1:15–16), and the Philistines' name for them here. Israel rarely calls itself this.

  • vv7–8 "A god has come… these mighty gods… with every kind of plague in the wilderness" — the Philistines know the Exodus story, but in their own terms: Elohim as many gods, and the plagues moved from Egypt to the wilderness. They are afraid for the right reason and tell the story wrong.

  • v13 "his heart trembled for the ark of God" — chared, the word of the fearful men sent home from Gideon's army (Judges 7:3). Eli fears for the ark before he fears for his sons. The written text has yakh, the reading yad, beside.

  • v15 "ninety-eight years old" — the Greek has ninety, and in v18 it has twenty years where the Hebrew has forty. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v18 "old and heavy" — kaved, heavy, from the root of kavod, honor, glory. The man of God warned Eli that he had given weight to his sons above the LORD (2:29–30).

  • vv21–22 "Ichabod… The glory has gone into exile" — I-khavod, where is the glory? or no glory. Galah, has gone into exile, is the word for a people carried off from its land. The glory, ha-kavod, has gone with the ark, and the dying mother names her son for the loss of it, not for the son. The Greek name is Ouai barchaboth, woe, Barchaboth.

  • v22 — the mother's last words repeat v21 without the husband and the father-in-law: only the ark.

chapters.title: The Ark Among the Philistines
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 5

Dagon

1The Philistines had taken the ark of God, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.

2The Philistines took the ark of God and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it up beside Dagon.

3When the people of Ashdod rose early the next day, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD. So they took Dagon and put him back in his place.

4But when they rose early the next morning, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the ark of the LORD, and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands lay cut off on the threshold. Only the trunk of Dagon was left to him.

5That is why the priests of Dagon and all who come into the house of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day.

The Hand of the LORD

6The hand of the LORD was heavy on the people of Ashdod. He devastated them and struck them with tumors, Ashdod and its territory, and mice sprang up in the middle of its land.

7When the men of Ashdod saw how it was, they said, "The ark of the God of Israel must not stay with us, for His hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god."

8So they sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines to them and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the God of Israel?" They said, "Let the ark of the God of Israel be moved around to Gath." So they moved the ark of the God of Israel there.

9And it came to pass, after they had moved it, that the hand of the LORD was against the city, with a very great confusion. He struck the men of the city, both small and great, and tumors broke out on them.

10So they sent the ark of God to Ekron. And it came to pass, when the ark of God came to Ekron, that the Ekronites cried out, "They have moved the ark of the God of Israel around to us, to kill us and our people!"

11They sent and gathered all the lords of the Philistines and said, "Send away the ark of the God of Israel, and let it return to its own place, so that it does not kill us and our people." For there was a deadly confusion throughout the whole city; the hand of God was very heavy there.

12The men who did not die were struck with tumors, and the cry of the city went up to heaven.

Notes

  • vv3–4 "Dagon had fallen on his face" — the posture of worship: the god of the Philistines lies face down before the ark, le-fanav artsah, as a worshipper would. The second morning he is broken, head and hands cut off, and only the trunk is left. Dagon was the god of the Philistines, and it was at a sacrifice to him in Gaza that Samson died (Judges 16:23–30).

  • v4 "Only the trunk of Dagon was left to him" — the Hebrew has only Dagon was left, what was Dagon: the body without head or hands. The Greek has only the back of Dagon was left.

  • v5 "do not tread on the threshold" — the fallen god's head and hands lay on the threshold, and the custom of stepping over it is explained by the story. To this day marks the narrator's own time.

  • vv6, 7, 11 "The hand of the LORD was heavy" — va-tikhbad yad YHWH, from kaved, heavy, the word of Eli's death (4:18) and of Ichabod's lost glory (4:21). The glory that went into exile from Israel is heavy on the Philistines.

  • vv6, 9, 12 "tumors" — the written text has ofalim, swellings, mounds; the reading tradition has techorim, a word of the same sense. The same pair stands in Deuteronomy 28:27, the boils of Egypt… tumors, one of the curses on Israel, and it falls here on Israel's enemy.

  • v6 "and mice sprang up in the middle of its land" — this clause is in the Greek, not the Hebrew. In the Hebrew the golden mice of 6:4–5 appear with no plague of mice told beforehand, though 6:5 speaks of your mice that ravage the land. The Greek keeps the detail the context calls for, and the text follows it (as also at 6:1).

  • v7 "His hand is hard on us and on Dagon our god" — the Philistines draw the conclusion the Exodus story drew: the LORD's judgment falls against all the gods of the land as well as its people (Exodus 12:12).

  • vv8–10 Ashdod, Gath, Ekron — three of the five Philistine cities (6:17). Each passes the ark on to the next, and the last cries out before it arrives.

  • v9 "a very great confusion" — mehumah, what the LORD brings on an enemy in battle: throw them into great confusion, mehumah gedolah (Deuteronomy 7:23). Here there is no battle, only the ark.

  • v12 "the cry of the city went up to heaven" — shav'at ha-ir, the cry for help. Israel cried out in Egypt, and the cry went up to God (Exodus 2:23). Now the cry is the Philistines'.

chapters.title: The Ark Returns
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 6

The Guilt Offering

1The ark of the LORD was in the country of the Philistines seven months, and their land swarmed with mice.

2The Philistines called for the priests and the soothsayers and said, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how we should send it back to its place."

3They said, "If you send away the ark of the God of Israel, do not send it empty, but be sure to return to Him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why His hand has not turned away from you."

4They said, "What is the guilt offering that we shall return to Him?" They said, "Five golden tumors and five golden mice, according to the number of the lords of the Philistines, for one plague was on all of you and on your lords.

5So you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that ravage the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps He will lighten His hand from you and from your gods and from your land.

6Why should you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When He had dealt harshly with them, did they not send the people away, and they went?

7And now take and prepare a new cart and two milk cows on which no yoke has come. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take their calves home, away from them.

8Take the ark of the LORD and put it on the cart, and put the golden objects that you are returning to Him as a guilt offering in a box beside it. Then send it off, and let it go.

9Watch: if it goes up by the road to its own territory, to Beth-shemesh, then it is He who has done us this great harm. But if not, then we will know that it was not His hand that struck us; it happened to us by chance."

Beth-shemesh

10The men did so. They took two milk cows and hitched them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.

11They put the ark of the LORD on the cart, and the box with the golden mice and the images of their tumors.

12The cows went straight along the road toward Beth-shemesh. They kept to one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. The lords of the Philistines went after them as far as the border of Beth-shemesh.

13The people of Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

14The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh and stopped there. A great stone was there. They split up the wood of the cart and offered the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

15The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the box that was with it, in which were the golden objects, and put them on the great stone. The men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and made sacrifices that day to the LORD.

16When the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron that day.

17These are the golden tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.

18The golden mice were according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both fortified cities and unwalled villages, as far as the great stone on which they set down the ark of the LORD, which is in the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh to this day.

19He struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh, because they looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck seventy men of the people, fifty thousand men. The people mourned, because the LORD had struck the people with a great slaughter.

20The men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? To whom shall He go up from us?"

21So they sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have brought back the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to you."

Notes

  • v1 "and their land swarmed with mice" — the clause is in the Greek; the Hebrew has only the seven months. As at 5:6, the text keeps the detail the Greek has, because v5 speaks of your mice that ravage the land and the Hebrew nowhere tells of them.

  • v3 "a guilt offering" — asham, the offering for a wrong done to what is holy (Leviticus 5:6). The Philistine priests know that the ark must not go back empty, reqam, the word of the law for Israel's pilgrims: They shall not appear before the face of the LORD empty-handed (Deuteronomy 16:16).

  • v5 "give glory to the God of Israel… lighten His hand" — kavod, glory, weight, and yaqel, make light. The LORD's hand has been heavy on them (5:6, 11); by giving Him weight they hope He will make it light.

  • v6 "Why should you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts?" — tekhabbedu, make heavy, the verb of Pharaoh, who made his own heart heavy (Exodus 8:15, 8:32). Dealt harshly, hit'allel, is the verb of Exodus 10:2, what I did in Egypt. The Philistine priests know the Exodus better than the Philistine soldiers did (4:8).

  • vv7–12 the test of the cows — two cows never yoked, like the red heifer… on which a yoke has never come (Numbers 19:2), and with their calves shut up at home. By nature they would turn back toward their calves. They go straight to Israel, lowing as they went, and do not turn aside to the right or to the left.

  • v9 "by chance" — miqreh, the word of Ruth 2:3, as it happened. The Philistines set a test to tell the hand of God from chance.

  • v14 "the field of Joshua of Beth-shemesh" — Beth-shemesh was a town of the Levites (Joshua 21:16), and v15 has the Levites handle the ark.

  • v17 "one for Ashdod, one for Gaza…" — the five cities of the five lords (Joshua 13:3; Judges 3:3).

  • v19 "because they looked into the ark… seventy men of the people, fifty thousand men" — to look on the holy things was death even for the Levites who carried them (Numbers 4:20). The Hebrew gives two numbers side by side, seventy men, fifty thousand men, without joining them; the Greek has the same, and adds that the sons of Jeconiah did not rejoice with the men of Beth-shemesh. The text gives the Hebrew as it stands.

  • v20 "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God?" — the question that the ark's journey has been asking of the Philistines is now asked in Israel.

chapters.title: Samuel Judges Israel
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 7

Kiriath-jearim

1The men of Kiriath-jearim came and took up the ark of the LORD and brought it into the house of Abinadab on the hill. They consecrated Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.

2And it came to pass, from the day that the ark stayed at Kiriath-jearim, that a long time passed, twenty years, and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.

Mizpah

3Samuel said to all the house of Israel, "If you are returning to the LORD with all your heart, put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, direct your hearts to the LORD and serve Him only, and He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines."

4So the sons of Israel put away the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served the LORD only.

5Samuel said, "Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD for you."

6They gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day, and said there, "We have sinned against the LORD." Samuel judged the sons of Israel at Mizpah.

7When the Philistines heard that the sons of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the sons of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.

8The sons of Israel said to Samuel, "Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, so that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines."

9Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. Samuel cried out to the LORD for Israel, and the LORD answered him.

10As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to fight against Israel. But the LORD thundered with a great voice that day against the Philistines and threw them into panic, and they were struck down before Israel.

11The men of Israel went out from Mizpah and pursued the Philistines and struck them down as far as below Beth-car.

Ebenezer

12Then Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, "Till now the LORD has helped us."

13So the Philistines were subdued and did not again enter the territory of Israel. The hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

14The cities that the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron to Gath, and Israel delivered their territory from the hand of the Philistines. There was peace also between Israel and the Amorites.

15Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

16He would go year by year on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah, and judge Israel in all these places.

17Then he would return to Ramah, for his home was there, and there he judged Israel. He built an altar there to the LORD.

Notes

  • v2 "twenty years… lamented after the LORD" — va-yinnahu, from nahah, to wail, to mourn, found rarely. The Greek has looked after the Lord. Either way, the twenty years end with Israel turning toward the LORD.

  • v3 "put away the foreign gods" — as Jacob said before Bethel, Remove the foreign gods that are among you (Genesis 35:2), and Joshua at the covenant, put away the foreign gods that are among you (Joshua 24:23). Each time the call comes before a new start.

  • v6 "drew water and poured it out before the LORD" — a rite found only here. Poured out, va-yishpekhu, is Hannah's verb: I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD (1:15). Samuel judged the sons of Israel: the first time the word judge is used of him.

  • v8 "Do not stop crying out" — al tacharesh mimmennu, do not be silent from us. Israel has learned in chapter 4 that the ark carried into battle does not save; now they ask for prayer.

  • v9 "a whole burnt offering" — olah kalil, the offering burned entire. The written text has va-ya'aleh, the reading va-ya'alehu; the meaning is the same.

  • v10 "the LORD thundered with a great voice… threw them into panic" — va-yar'em, the word of Hannah's song, against them He thunders in the heavens (2:10). Va-yehummem is the verb of Exodus 14:24 and Judges 4:15: the LORD throws the enemy into panic, and Israel only pursues.

  • v12 "Ebenezer… Till now the LORD has helped us" — even ha-ezer, stone of help. The name was used in 4:1 for the place of Israel's defeat; here it is given, at the site of a victory. Shen is tooth, a crag; the Greek reads the old one, yeshanah.

  • v13 "did not again enter the territory of Israel" — the verse speaks of Samuel's days. Saul will fight the Philistines through his whole reign (14:52), and Goliath is a Philistine.

  • v14 "peace also between Israel and the Amorites" — the peoples of the hill country, not the Philistines of the coast.

  • vv15–17 "a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal and Mizpah" — the three places of Israel's old assemblies (Judges 20:1, 20:18; Joshua 5:9–10). He built an altar there: Shiloh is no longer spoken of after chapter 4, and Samuel worships at Ramah.

chapters.title: Israel Asks for a King
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 8

Samuel's Sons

1And it came to pass, when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel.

2The name of his firstborn son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.

3But his sons did not walk in his ways. They turned aside after gain, took bribes and perverted justice.

"Give Us a King"

4Then all the elders of Israel gathered together and came to Samuel at Ramah.

5They said to him, "You are old, and your sons do not walk in your ways. Now appoint for us a king to judge us like all the nations."

6But the thing was evil in Samuel's eyes when they said, "Give us a king to judge us." Samuel prayed to the LORD.

7The LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to the voice of the people in all that they say to you, for they have not rejected you; they have rejected Me from being king over them.

8According to all the deeds they have done from the day I brought them up from Egypt until this day, forsaking Me and serving other gods, so they are doing to you also.

9And now, listen to their voice. Only you shall solemnly warn them and tell them the ways of the king who will reign over them."

The Ways of the King

10So Samuel told all the words of the LORD to the people who were asking him for a king.

11He said, "These will be the ways of the king who will reign over you: he will take your sons and put them to his chariots and among his horsemen, and they will run before his chariots.

12He will appoint for himself commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties, and some to plow his ground and to reap his harvest, and to make his weapons of war and the equipment of his chariots.

13He will take your daughters to be perfumers and cooks and bakers.

14He will take the best of your fields and vineyards and olive groves and give them to his servants.

15He will take a tenth of your grain and of your vineyards and give it to his officials and his servants.

16He will take your male servants and your female servants, and the best of your young men, and your donkeys, and put them to his work.

17He will take a tenth of your flocks, and you yourselves will be his slaves.

18In that day you will cry out because of your king, whom you have chosen for yourselves, but the LORD will not answer you in that day."

19But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel. They said, "No! There shall be a king over us,

20so that we too may be like all the nations, and our king may judge us and go out before us and fight our battles."

21When Samuel had heard all the words of the people, he repeated them in the ears of the LORD.

22The LORD said to Samuel, "Listen to their voice and make them a king." Then Samuel said to the men of Israel, "Go, each to his town."

Notes

  • v3 "turned aside after gain, took bribes and perverted justice" — each of the three is forbidden in the law: You shall not bend judgment… and you shall not take a bribe (Deuteronomy 16:19). Samuel's sons repeat Eli's sons (2:12–17), in the courts instead of at the altar.

  • v5 "a king to judge us like all the nations" — the words Deuteronomy 17:14 foresaw: Let me set a king over me, like all the nations that are around me. The law allows a king, with limits; the elders ask for one for the reason the law names.

  • v7 "they have rejected Me from being king over them" — Gideon had refused to rule: The LORD will rule over you (Judges 8:23). The request for a king is heard by the LORD as a request for a replacement.

  • v9 "the ways of the king" — mishpat ha-melekh, the justice or the rule of the king. Mishpat is what the elders say they want from him, to judge us, le-shoftenu (v5); what Samuel describes is what the king will take.

  • vv11–17 "he will take" — yiqqach, four times, and ya'sor, he will take a tenth, twice. The tenth the law gives to the LORD and the Levites the king will take for himself and his servants. The list ends where Israel began: you yourselves will be his slaves (v17), avadim, the word of Egypt.

  • v12 "commanders of thousands and commanders of fifties" — the officers Moses set over the people (Exodus 18:21), now made the king's.

  • v16 "the best of your young men" — bachureikhem. The Greek has your cattle, beqarkhem, which fits a list of servants and donkeys; the Hebrew letters differ by one. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v18 "you will cry out… but the LORD will not answer you" — in Judges the pattern was the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer (Judges 3:9). Here the cry is foreseen, and the answer refused.

  • v20 "go out before us and fight our battles" — Israel's battles in Judges and at Mizpah (7:10) were the LORD's. The people now ask for a man to fight them.

  • v22 "Listen to their voice" — the LORD grants the request He has called a rejection of Himself.

chapters.title: Saul and the Lost Donkeys
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 9

The Search

1There was a man of Benjamin whose name was Kish son of Abiel, son of Zeror, son of Becorath, son of Aphiah, a Benjaminite, a man of worth.

2He had a son whose name was Saul, a choice young man and handsome. There was no man among the sons of Israel more handsome than he; from his shoulders upward he was taller than any of the people.

3The donkeys of Kish, Saul's father, were lost. Kish said to Saul his son, "Take one of the young men with you, and arise, go and look for the donkeys."

4He passed through the hill country of Ephraim and through the land of Shalishah, but they did not find them. They passed through the land of Shaalim, but they were not there. Then he passed through the land of Benjamin, but they did not find them.

5When they came to the land of Zuph, Saul said to his young man who was with him, "Come, let us go back, or my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and become anxious about us."

6But he said to him, "There is a man of God in this town, and the man is held in honor; all that he says comes true. Let us go there now. Perhaps he can tell us about the journey we have set out on."

7Saul said to his young man, "But if we go, what shall we bring the man? For the bread in our sacks is gone, and there is no gift to bring to the man of God. What do we have?"

8The young man answered Saul again and said, "I have a quarter of a shekel of silver with me. I will give it to the man of God, and he will tell us our way."

9(Formerly in Israel, when a man went to inquire of God, he would say, "Come, let us go to the seer," for the one who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer.)

10Saul said to his young man, "Well said. Come, let us go." So they went to the town where the man of God was.

Samuel

11As they went up the ascent to the town, they met young women coming out to draw water, and said to them, "Is the seer here?"

12They answered them, "He is; he is just ahead of you. Hurry now, for he has come to the town today, because the people have a sacrifice today on the high place.

13As soon as you enter the town you will find him, before he goes up to the high place to eat, for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice; afterward those who are invited eat. So go up now, for you will find him about this time."

14So they went up to the town. As they were entering the town, Samuel was coming out toward them on his way up to the high place.

15Now a day before Saul came, the LORD had revealed to Samuel:

16"About this time tomorrow I will send you a man from the land of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be leader over My people Israel. He will save My people from the hand of the Philistines, for I have seen My people, because their cry has come to Me."

17When Samuel saw Saul, the LORD told him, "There is the man of whom I spoke to you! He shall restrain My people."

18Saul came up to Samuel in the gateway and said, "Please tell me where the seer's house is."

19Samuel answered Saul, "I am the seer. Go up before me to the high place, for you shall eat with me today, and in the morning I will let you go and will tell you all that is in your heart.

20As for your donkeys that were lost three days ago, do not set your heart on them, for they have been found. On whom is all the desire of Israel? Is it not on you and on all your father's house?"

21Saul answered, "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel? Is not my clan the least of all the clans of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then have you spoken to me like this?"

The Meal at the High Place

22Samuel took Saul and his young man and brought them into the hall and gave them a place at the head of those who had been invited, about thirty men.

23Samuel said to the cook, "Bring the portion I gave you, of which I said to you, 'Put it aside.'"

24So the cook took up the thigh and what was on it and set it before Saul. Samuel said, "See, what was kept is set before you. Eat, for it has been kept for you until the appointed time, since I said, 'I have invited the people.'" So Saul ate with Samuel that day.

25When they came down from the high place into the town, he spoke with Saul on the roof.

26They rose early, and at the break of dawn Samuel called to Saul on the roof, "Get up, and I will send you on your way." Saul got up, and both of them, he and Samuel, went outside.

27As they were going down to the edge of the town, Samuel said to Saul, "Tell the young man to go on ahead of us." When he had gone on, Samuel said, "But you stand still for a while, so that I may make you hear the word of God."

Notes

  • v1 "a man of worth" — gibbor chayil, as Boaz is described in Ruth 2:1: a man of wealth and standing. The written text has mi-ben yamin, from a son of the right hand, and the reading mi-Binyamin, from Benjamin; the meaning is the same.

  • v2 "a choice young man and handsome… taller than any of the people" — bachur va-tov. The chapter introduces Saul by his looks and height; 16:7 will set that measure aside, the LORD looks on the heart. Saul, Sha'ul, is asked for: the people asked Samuel for a king (8:10), and this is the one asked for.

  • v6 "all that he says comes true" — bo yavo, the report of 3:19: the LORD let none of Samuel's words fall to the ground.

  • v9 "the one who is now called a prophet was formerly called a seer" — the narrator explains an old word for his readers, as Ruth 4:7 explained an old custom. Ro'eh, seer, is from ra'ah, to see.

  • v16 "anoint him to be leader… for I have seen My people, because their cry has come to Me" — nagid, leader, not melekh, king; the LORD does not use the people's word. Their cry has come to Me are the words of the LORD at the bush: the cry of the sons of Israel has come to Me (Exodus 3:9). The king is sent as a deliverer, as Moses was.

  • v17 "He shall restrain My people" — ya'tsor, hold back, restrain, an unusual word for ruling. The Greek has he shall rule.

  • v20 "on whom is all the desire of Israel?" — chemdat Yisra'el, what Israel longs for. Samuel answers a question about donkeys with a hint of a kingdom.

  • v21 "Am I not a Benjaminite, from the smallest of the tribes of Israel?" — Benjamin was nearly destroyed in Judges 20–21. The answer is Gideon's, My clan is the weakest in Manasseh (Judges 6:15).

  • v24 "the thigh and what was on it" — ha-shoq, the portion the law gives the priest from a peace offering (Leviticus 7:32). Samuel sets the priest's portion before Saul. Since I said, 'I have invited the people' is compressed in the Hebrew; the Greek has it was set before you as a witness, above the others.

  • v25 "he spoke with Saul on the roof" — va-yedabber. The Greek has they spread a bed for Saul on the roof, and he slept, which fits v26, where Samuel calls to Saul on the roof at dawn. The text follows the Hebrew.

chapters.title: Saul Anointed and Chosen
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 10

The Anointing

1Then Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said, "Has not the LORD anointed you leader over His people Israel? You shall reign over the people of the LORD and save them from the hand of their enemies all around. This shall be the sign to you that the LORD has anointed you leader over His inheritance:

2When you leave me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will say to you, 'The donkeys you went to look for have been found. Your father has stopped caring about the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'

3Then you will go on from there and come to the oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.

4They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall accept from their hand.

5After that you will come to Gibeath-elohim, where the Philistine garrison is. And it shall come to pass, as you come there to the town, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, with harp, tambourine, flute and lyre before them, and they will be prophesying.

6Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush on you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.

7And it shall come to pass, when these signs come to you, that you shall do whatever you find to do, for God is with you.

8Then go down before me to Gilgal. I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait, until I come to you and show you what you are to do."

The Signs

9When he turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all these signs came to pass that day.

10When they came there to Gibeah, a band of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God rushed on him, and he prophesied among them.

11When all who had known him before saw him prophesying with the prophets, the people said to one another, "What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"

12A man from there answered, "But who is their father?" So it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

13When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.

14Saul's uncle said to him and to his young man, "Where did you go?" He said, "To look for the donkeys. When we saw that they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel."

15Saul's uncle said, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."

16Saul said to his uncle, "He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found." But about the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.

The Lot at Mizpah

17Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.

18He said to the sons of Israel, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.'

19But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and distresses, and you have said to Him, 'No, set a king over us.' So now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands."

20Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

21He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken. Then he brought the clan of the Matrites near man by man, and Saul son of Kish was taken. But when they looked for him, he could not be found.

22So they inquired of the LORD again, "Has the man come here yet?" The LORD said, "He is hiding among the baggage."

23They ran and took him from there, and when he stood among the people, he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upward.

24Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? There is none like him among all the people." All the people shouted and said, "Long live the king!"

25Then Samuel told the people the rule of the kingship and wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each to his home.

26Saul also went home to Gibeah, and with him went the men of valor whose hearts God had touched.

27But some worthless men said, "How can this man save us?" They despised him and brought him no gift. But he kept silent.

Notes

  • v1 "You shall reign over the people of the LORD… And this shall be the sign to you" — these words are in the Greek and not in the Hebrew, whose verse ends with Has not the LORD anointed you leader over His inheritance? The Greek names the sign that vv2–7 go on to give (when these signs come to you, v7); the Hebrew never introduces it. The phrase anointed you… leader stands twice in the Greek, and the Hebrew has only the second, as if the eye had passed from the first to the second. The text follows the Greek.

  • v1 "the flask of oil… anointed you leader" — nagid, as in 9:16. This is the first anointing of a king in Israel; the flask, pakh, is the same word used when Elisha sends one of the sons of the prophets with this flask of oil to anoint Jehu (2 Kings 9:1).

  • v2 "Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah" — Genesis 35:19–20 puts the grave on the road to Ephrath, where Jacob set up a pillar to this day. Saul, a son of Rachel's son Benjamin, begins his road at her grave.

  • v5 "Gibeath-elohim, where the Philistine garrison is" — the hill of God, held by a Philistine netsiv, a garrison or an officer. The Greek reads Nasib the Philistine, as a man's name. The new king's first task is in sight on the first day.

  • vv6, 10 "the Spirit of the LORD will rush on you… be turned into another man" — tsalach, the verb of the Spirit on Samson (Judges 14:6). In v9 God gave him another heart: the change is given before he has done anything.

  • vv11–12 "Is Saul also among the prophets?… But who is their father?" — the proverb is given twice in the book, here and at 19:24, with two different stories. Who is their father? seems to mean that prophets have no pedigree, so a wealthy man's son is out of place among them. The Greek has his father.

  • v16 "But about the matter of the kingdom… he did not tell him" — the first of Saul's silences; v22 finds him hiding, and v27 has him keep silent before his mockers.

  • v19 "you have rejected your God, who saves you" — Samuel repeats the LORD's word of 8:7 to the people's faces. The lot then falls exactly as the LORD has already chosen (9:16).

  • v21 "Then he brought the clan of the Matrites near man by man" — this step is in the Greek; the Hebrew passes from the clan to Saul at once. The same order of tribe, clan, and man is followed when Achan is taken by lot (Joshua 7:16–18). The text follows the Greek.

  • v25 "the rule of the kingship… wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD" — mishpat ha-melukhah, set against the ways of the king of 8:11, which describe what a king takes. The written law of the king recalls Deuteronomy 17:18, where the king writes a copy of this instruction in a book.

speech.text: 1 Samuel 10
The Anointing

Then Samuel took the flask of oil and poured it on his head and kissed him and said, "Has not the LORD anointed you leader over His people Israel? You shall reign over the people of the LORD and save them from the hand of their enemies all around. This shall be the sign to you that the LORD has anointed you leader over His inheritance:

When you leave me today, you will find two men by Rachel's tomb in the territory of Benjamin at Zelzah. They will say to you, 'The donkeys you went to look for have been found. Your father has stopped caring about the donkeys and is anxious about you, saying, "What shall I do about my son?"'

Then you will go on from there and come to the oak of Tabor. Three men going up to God at Bethel will meet you there, one carrying three young goats, another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a skin of wine.
They will greet you and give you two loaves of bread, which you shall accept from their hand.

After that you will come to Gibeath-elohim, where the Philistine garrison is. And it shall come to pass, as you come there to the town, that you will meet a band of prophets coming down from the high place, with harp, tambourine, flute and lyre before them, and they will be prophesying.
Then the Spirit of the LORD will rush on you, and you will prophesy with them and be turned into another man.
And it shall come to pass, when these signs come to you, that you shall do whatever you find to do, for God is with you.
Then go down before me to Gilgal. I will come down to you to offer burnt offerings and to sacrifice peace offerings. Seven days you shall wait, until I come to you and show you what you are to do."
The Signs
When he turned his back to go from Samuel, God gave him another heart, and all these signs came to pass that day.
When they came there to Gibeah, a band of prophets met him, and the Spirit of God rushed on him, and he prophesied among them.
When all who had known him before saw him prophesying with the prophets, the people said to one another, "What has happened to the son of Kish? Is Saul also among the prophets?"
A man from there answered, "But who is their father?" So it became a proverb: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"
When he had finished prophesying, he came to the high place.
Saul's uncle said to him and to his young man, "Where did you go?" He said, "To look for the donkeys. When we saw that they were nowhere to be found, we went to Samuel."
Saul's uncle said, "Please tell me what Samuel said to you."
Saul said to his uncle, "He told us plainly that the donkeys had been found." But about the matter of the kingdom, of which Samuel had spoken, he did not tell him.
The Lot at Mizpah
Samuel called the people together to the LORD at Mizpah.

He said to the sons of Israel, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: 'I brought Israel up from Egypt, and I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all the kingdoms that oppressed you.'

But today you have rejected your God, who saves you from all your troubles and distresses, and you have said to Him, 'No, set a king over us.' So now present yourselves before the LORD by your tribes and by your thousands."
Samuel brought all the tribes of Israel near, and the tribe of Benjamin was taken.

He brought the tribe of Benjamin near by its clans, and the clan of the Matrites was taken. Then he brought the clan of the Matrites near man by man, and Saul son of Kish was taken. But when they looked for him, he could not be found.
So they inquired of the LORD again, "Has the man come here yet?" The LORD said, "He is hiding among the baggage."
They ran and took him from there, and when he stood among the people, he was taller than any of the people from his shoulders upward.
Samuel said to all the people, "Do you see the one whom the LORD has chosen? There is none like him among all the people." All the people shouted and said, "Long live the king!"
Then Samuel told the people the rule of the kingship and wrote it in a book and laid it up before the LORD. Then Samuel sent all the people away, each to his home.
Saul also went home to Gibeah, and with him went the men of valor whose hearts God had touched.
But some worthless men said, "How can this man save us?" They despised him and brought him no gift. But he kept silent.

chapters.title: Saul Rescues Jabesh-gilead
chapters.html:
1 Samuel 11

Nahash

1Nahash the Ammonite went up and camped against Jabesh-gilead. All the men of Jabesh said to Nahash, "Make a covenant with us, and we will serve you."

2But Nahash the Ammonite said to them, "On this condition I will make a covenant with you: that I gouge out every right eye of yours, and so bring disgrace on all Israel."

3The elders of Jabesh said to him, "Give us seven days, so that we may send messengers through all the territory of Israel. Then, if there is no one to save us, we will come out to you."

4When the messengers came to Gibeah of Saul, they told the news in the hearing of the people, and all the people lifted up their voices and wept.

Saul Rises

5Just then Saul was coming behind the oxen from the field. Saul said, "What is wrong with the people, that they are weeping?" So they told him the words of the men of Jabesh.

6The Spirit of God rushed on Saul when he heard these words, and his anger burned hot.

7He took a pair of oxen and cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel by the hand of the messengers, saying, "Whoever does not come out after Saul and after Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!" The dread of the LORD fell on the people, and they came out as one man.

8He mustered them at Bezek. The sons of Israel were three hundred thousand, and the men of Judah thirty thousand.

9They said to the messengers who had come, "Say this to the men of Jabesh-gilead: 'Tomorrow, by the time the sun is hot, you shall have deliverance.'" When the messengers came and told the men of Jabesh, they rejoiced.

10So the men of Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will come out to you, and you may do to us whatever seems good in your eyes."

11The next day Saul put the people in three companies. They came into the middle of the camp in the morning watch and struck down the Ammonites until the heat of the day. Those who survived were scattered, so that no two of them were left together.

The Kingdom Renewed

12Then the people said to Samuel, "Who is it that said, 'Shall Saul reign over us?' Give us the men, so that we may put them to death."

13But Saul said, "No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked deliverance in Israel."

14Samuel said to the people, "Come, let us go to Gilgal and renew the kingdom there."

15So all the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal. There they offered peace offerings before the LORD, and there Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly.

Notes

  • v1 "Nahash the Ammonite… Jabesh-gilead" — Nachash is serpent. Jabesh-gilead is the town that sent no one to Mizpah and was destroyed by Israel to find wives for Benjamin (Judges 21:8–14); Saul is a Benjaminite, and his first act as king is to save it. It will also be the town that buries him (31:11–13). The Greek opens the verse with And it came to pass about a month later, reading the last words of 10:27 (but he kept silent, ke-macharish) as about a month, ke-mechodesh: the letters differ by one.

  • v2 "gouge out every right eye… disgrace on all Israel" — Nahash says why: the mutilation is meant as a disgrace, cherpah, for all Israel, not only Jabesh. The town's surrender is to be a sign of Israel's helplessness.

  • v5 "Saul was coming behind the oxen from the field" — the anointed king is still plowing. The oxen he walks behind are the ones he will cut up in v7.

  • v6 "The Spirit of God rushed on Saul… his anger burned hot" — va-titslach, as in 10:6, 10:10, and as on Samson (Judges 14:6). This time the Spirit comes with anger, and the anger goes into a rescue.

  • v7 "cut them in pieces and sent them throughout all the territory of Israel" — the words of Judges 19:29, where the Levite cut up his concubine and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel. That summons began a war against Benjamin; this one, from a Benjaminite, rescues the town that paid for that war. As one man, as the tribes came out in Judges 20:1.

  • v8 "The sons of Israel… and the men of Judah" — Judah is counted apart from the rest of Israel, the first time the book does so. The Greek has six hundred thousand and seventy thousand.

  • v10 "Tomorrow we will come out to you" — the men of Jabesh tell Nahash what he wants to hear, and it is true in a way he does not expect: they come out with Saul's army.

  • v11 "three companies… in the morning watch" — Gideon's three companies (Judges 7:16), and the hour when the LORD looked down on the camp of Egypt and threw it into panic (Exodus 14:24).

  • vv12–13 "No one shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has worked deliverance" — the men who despised Saul (10:27) are spared by him, and he credits the rescue to the LORD. The Greek of v12 has Who is it that said, "Saul shall not reign over us"?

  • vv14–15 "renew the kingdom… made Saul king before the LORD in Gilgal" — the third step in Saul's making, after the private anointing (10:1) and the lot at Mizpah (10:24). Gilgal is where Israel first camped in the land (Joshua 4:19). The Greek has Samuel anointed Saul king there.
